book.title: Ibn Jubayr: A Great Traveler from Al-Andalus (A1)

pages.title: Al-Andalus
pages.content:
From 711 to 1492, Muslims lived in Spain and Portugal. The name of this place was Al-Andalus. Muslims, Christians and Jews lived there together. They worked and studied together.

People in Al-Andalus made beautiful houses, gardens and pictures. They wrote important books. They were good at medicine and science. For example, Ibn Rushd was a doctor and a scientist. Ibn Tufayl was a doctor and a writer, too. He wrote books.

Al-Andalus had big, beautiful cities. Córdoba was the biggest city in Western Europe. Granada and Seville were big cities, too.

Ibn Jubayr was born in Valencia in 1145. Valencia is a city in Spain, near the sea.

pages.title: Three Great Travelers
pages.content:
Do you know Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta? They were great travelers. Ibn Jubayr was a great traveler, too.

Ibn Jubayr traveled from 1183 to 1185. His trip was about 15,000 kilometers. Marco Polo went about 24,000 kilometers, and Ibn Battuta’s journey was 117,000 kilometers!

Ibn Jubayr did not go very far. But he wrote one of the first travel books in the world. Ibn Battuta read his book, too.

A time when you go to a place and come back.

pages.title: A Young Man from Valencia
pages.content:
When he was young, Ibn Jubayr studied hard. He learned about Islam, languages and books. Then he got a job in Granada. He was a secretary for the ruler of Granada.

He had a big dream. He wanted to go on Hajj. He also wanted to see other Muslim countries and learn new things. He wanted to see Baghdad, Aleppo, Jerusalem and Damascus.

In 1183, he started his long journey. He was 38 years old.

pages.title: The Rihla
pages.content:
Many people from Al-Andalus went on Hajj. But Ibn Jubayr did something new. He took a diary with him. He wrote in it every day. He wrote about people and cities.

After the journey, his diary became a book. Its name is the Rihla. Rihla is the Arabic word for “journey”. The book made Ibn Jubayr famous. Later, other travelers wrote similar books.

In those days, travel was very hard and dangerous. Ibn Jubayr went on ships, on camels and on foot. His journey was more than two years long.

pages.title: A Storm at Sea
pages.content:
On February 3, 1183, Ibn Jubayr left Granada. He went to Ceuta in North Africa. There, he got on a ship. The ship went past Sardinia and Sicily. During his journey, Ibn Jubayr had many interesting moments and some dangerous ones.

Near Sardinia, he saw 80 Muslim prisoners. Ibn Jubayr was very sad.

Then a very bad storm came. The people on the ship were afraid. But the ship and the people were all safe. Then the ship went to Crete and then to Egypt.

On March 26, the ship came to Alexandria.

pages.title: The Lighthouse of Alexandria
pages.content:
In Alexandria, he went to see the famous lighthouse of Alexandria. It was very tall and very old. Ibn Jubayr wrote, “It is taller than 50 men!” He thought it was amazing.

After eight days, he went to Cairo.

pages.title: Cairo and Saladin
pages.content:
In Cairo, the ruler was Sultan Saladin. Ibn Jubayr had great respect for him. Saladin was kind and fair. He took care of mosques, schools and hospitals. The roads were safe day and night.

Ibn Jubayr visited a big hospital in Cairo. It was free for all people. It had different rooms for men and for women. He saw the pyramids, too.

Saladin also opened houses for students, teachers and poor people. They lived there, and they got food and clothes. Saladin did not forget poor people, either. Every day, he gave 2,000 loaves of bread to poor people.

pages.title: Eight Months in Mecca
pages.content:
From Egypt, Ibn Jubayr traveled with a caravan of camels. Ibn Jubayr wrote, “Some tents in the caravan are so big and beautiful. They are like moving palaces!”

In August 1183, he came to Mecca. He stayed there for more than eight months. He made the Hajj. He visited the Ka’ba with great love and respect. People came to Mecca from Persia, India and Africa.

In his book, he wrote about Mecca: “Mecca is a small place between mountains. But thousands of people can stay there together. This is a great wonder from Allah. Doctors say Mecca and a mother’s body are similar. A mother’s body grows and makes a place for her baby. It is the same for Mecca. Even the biggest city in the world cannot hold this many people.”

vocabulary.definition: A group of people and animals on a journey.
A small house of cloth; you can move it.

pages.title: Medina, Baghdad and Damascus
pages.content:
On April 16, 1184, Ibn Jubayr went to Medina. He stayed there for five nights. Then he went across the desert with a big caravan. He went to Baghdad.

Baghdad was a very big city. Ibn Jubayr wrote, “Baghdad has 2,000 baths and 11 big mosques.”

Then he went to Aleppo and Damascus. In Damascus, he saw the Great Mosque. He wrote about its doors, its towers and its beautiful walls.

In Damascus, students and travelers stayed in schools for free. Travel was easy for them there.

vocabulary.definition: A big, dry place with sand and very little water.
The biggest and most important mosque of a city.
A tall, thin building or part of a building.
And you do not pay money.

pages.title: Acre and the Way Home
pages.content:
Next, Ibn Jubayr went to Acre. Acre is a city near the sea. He waited there for about two weeks. He needed a good wind for the ship.

Then he got on a ship with 50 Muslims and many Christians. There were big storms again. Near Sicily, the ship hit the ground and stopped. It could not move. Ibn Jubayr was in great danger. But finally, he was safe. William II, the king of Sicily, helped the people from the ship. The king knew Arabic!

vocabulary.definition: Air that moves.
Go into a ship, a bus or a train.

A man; he is the head of a country.

pages.title: Home Again
pages.content:
Ibn Jubayr waited in Sicily for good weather. Then he got on a new ship. In 1185, he came back to Spain. He was home again!

His journey was two years and three and a half months long. It was dangerous. On the sea, there were storms. In the desert, there were thieves. The sun was very hot, and people needed water.

In the end, he was safe back home. He thanked Allah.

Must have.
Say "thank you".

pages.title: Lessons from a Journey
pages.content:
Back in Granada, Ibn Jubayr finished his book, Rihla. He also taught the hadiths. Hadiths are the words of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh).

After that, he went to Mecca two more times. In the end, he lived in Alexandria. He died there in 1217.

Ibn Jubayr’s first goal was the Hajj. But his journey gave him much more. He saw many cities. He met Muslims from many countries. He learned many new things. He did not find these things at home.

Ibn Jubayr said to young people, “Travel and learn!”

places.name: Valencia
places.text: Ibn Jubayr was born in Valencia in 1145. Valencia is a city in Spain, near the sea.
places.teacherNote: Chapters 1 and 3. At that time, Valencia was a part of Al-Andalus.
places.question: When was Ibn Jubayr born?

places.name: Granada
places.text: Ibn Jubayr worked in Granada. He was a secretary for the ruler of Granada. He left Granada on February 3, 1183. Back in Granada, he finished his book.
places.teacherNote: Chapters 3, 5 and 12. Granada is the start and the end of the journey.
places.question: What was Ibn Jubayr’s job in Granada?

places.name: Ceuta
places.text: Ceuta is a city in North Africa. There, Ibn Jubayr got on a ship.
places.teacherNote: Chapter 5. The book does not say how he went from Granada to Ceuta, so this part of the line is only a guide.
places.question: What did Ibn Jubayr get on in Ceuta?

places.name: Sicily
places.text: Sicily is a big island. The ship went past Sicily. On the way home, the ship hit the ground near Sicily. William II, the king of Sicily, helped the people from the ship.
places.teacherNote: Chapters 5, 10 and 11. The book does not name the place of the accident, so the map marks the whole island.
places.question: Who helped the people from the ship?

places.name: Alexandria
places.text: On March 26, the ship came to Alexandria. Ibn Jubayr saw the famous lighthouse. It was very tall and very old. In the end, he lived in Alexandria and died there in 1217.
places.teacherNote: Chapters 5, 6 and 12. The sea line is only a guide.
places.question: What did Ibn Jubayr see in Alexandria?

places.name: Cairo
places.text: In Cairo, the ruler was Sultan Saladin. Ibn Jubayr visited a big hospital. It was free for all people. He saw the pyramids, too.
places.question: Who was the ruler in Cairo?

places.name: Mecca
places.text: Ibn Jubayr came to Mecca in August 1183. He stayed there for more than eight months. He made the Hajj.
places.teacherNote: Chapter 8. The book names no stops between Egypt and Mecca, so the line is only a guide.
places.question: How long did Ibn Jubayr stay in Mecca?

places.name: Medina
places.text: On April 16, 1184, Ibn Jubayr went to Medina. He stayed there for five nights.
places.question: How many nights did Ibn Jubayr stay in Medina?

places.name: Baghdad
places.text: Ibn Jubayr went across the desert to Baghdad. He wrote, “Baghdad has 2,000 baths and 11 big mosques.”
places.teacherNote: Chapter 9. The line through the desert is only a guide.
places.question: How many baths did Baghdad have?

places.name: Aleppo
places.text: After Baghdad, Ibn Jubayr went to Aleppo.
places.question: Where did Ibn Jubayr go after Baghdad?

places.name: Damascus
places.text: In Damascus, Ibn Jubayr saw the Great Mosque. He wrote about its doors, its towers and its beautiful walls.
places.teacherNote: Chapter 9. Students and travelers stayed in schools here for free.
places.question: What did Ibn Jubayr see in Damascus?

places.name: Acre
places.text: Acre is a city near the sea. Ibn Jubayr waited here for about two weeks. He needed a good wind for the ship.
places.question: Why did Ibn Jubayr wait in Acre?

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
